key_insight: AI agents could deepen societal inequality when people differ in access to them, their quality, or how many they can use. This paper offers a conceptual framework for understanding these risks and shaping future research.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of identifying how unequal access to AI agents—and differences in agent capabilities and numbers—could create or amplify societal inequalities.
method: Develops a conceptual framework to identify potential sources of agent-driven inequality.
Examines differences in access, quality, and number of AI agents.
Proposes a research agenda to help understand and address these societal risks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the framework highlights why agent access and deployment choices deserve attention alongside technical performance. It can guide questions about who benefits from agentic systems and who may be left behind.
visual_elements: Three-axis diagram showing access, agent quality, and number of agents as dimensions of inequality.
Side-by-side illustration of people supported by different numbers and capabilities of AI agents.
Conceptual flowchart linking unequal agent resources to potential disparities in societal outcomes.
Research roadmap connecting identified inequality risks to questions for future investigation.
paper_authors: Matthew Sharp, Omer Bilgin, Iason Gabriel, Lewis Hammond
